This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the
Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned Lac no. 105/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/Dc(Nw))
Ram Narain v. Union of India Page no. 2 of 15 aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded
by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the Lac') for acquisition of their
land for public purpose.

sentences.text:
The petition was filed before the Lac and referred to by the Collector for
determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification
bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/La/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under
Section 4 of the Act, intended to acquire about 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas of land with its specification
mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the
"Planned Development of Delhi".

3. The Government vide consequent declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/La/28176
dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2480 Bigha 01
Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate
of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.

The Lac (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as
provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 U/s 11 of
the Act in respect of 2480 Bighas 01 Biswas out of the aforesaid acquired land and awarded a
compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for
the entire acquired land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

It is stated that the petitioners have accepted the award amount without prejudice to its rights
and has not received the compensation till the filing of the present petition and the petitioners shall
accept the award amount under protest.

The Award passed by the learned Lac is highly inadequate
and insufficient and not in accordance w
ith the market value prevailing on the date of the notification under section 4 of the Act.

The petitioners have made appearance before the learned LAC and filed representation and put forth their grievance in writing for enhancement of compensation, however, they were not called for negotiation.
LAC no. 105/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ram Narain v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 15 7.

sentences.text:
As such the present reference petition has been filed on the following grounds :
(i) The learned LAC has not adopted the correct method for calculation the correct valuation of the said land and has made grave error in holding/assessing the market value of the said land based on the old policy of the Government.

The learned LAC has not appreciated the judgment of the superior Courts wherein, it has been observed that "value cannot be so fixed on the information given by the outside Authority or booklet or directory issued by the Government.
The market value of the acquired land is only to be determined by keeping in view the marketability and potentiality of the land".
It is, therefore, prayed that the value of the said land is to be reassessed and to be determined strictly as provided under the law.

(ii) It is stated that the award has been pronounced on 14.09.2005, however, physical possession of the said land has not been taken but the interest has been calculated up to date of award, which should have been taken to the date of payment, therefore, the petitioners have to lose heavy amount of interest on this account.

(iii) The learned LAC has also erred in not including the cost of the crop prevailing on the date of taking physical possession and the whole of the crop of the petitioners were destroyed without giving them opportunity to cut the crop.

No notice for taking the position has been LAC no. 105/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ram Narain v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 15 given to the petitioners, therefore, the petitioners have suffered loss on account of destruction of his crops.

entities.text: Ram Narain v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iv) The learned LAC has also made error in assessing the market value of the said land without considering potentiality of the land as mandated by the Hon'ble superior courts whereby, it has been observed that the prospects and possibilities of future development i.e. potentiality ought to be taken into account in assessing the market value.
Potentiality means such used to which the land to be put in the near reasonable future.

It is the duty of the LAC to take into consideration every intrinsic Ram Narain (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 6 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180654263/
3 quality and intrinsic circumstances which tends to push the value either up or down.

sentences.text: (v) The learned LAC has not taken into account the market value which has been fixed by the Government and to be charged from the allottees of the residential plot/flats.

The market value was fixed by the Government at the time of notification under Section 4 of the Act without adjustment of amount towards the development charges, however, on the contrary, market value should have been assessed after taking into account the development charges.

The DDA has issued the guidelines/circulars showing the statement of market rates or charging unearned increase for the Colonies under the control of DDA year wise, however, the assessment of market value of the said land has been taken without consideration of the guidelines.

The DDA LAC no. 105/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ram Narain v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 15 and the said land has raised the rate of alternative plots from Rs. 750 per square yards to Rs. 4000 per square yards,
therefore, it is clear that the rates were increased by DDA and the said land has a very high potential value, which is evident from the said effect, that the price of the said land has increasing trend as regarding its market value and after afixation of the rate of agricultural land in Delhi, the prices of the said land has been increased by almost five times.
(vi) The learned LAC has also made grave error by not calling the petitioners for negotiation and the decision has been taken arbitrarily which is against the principles of natural justice.

(vii) The Municipal Corporation of Delhi has allotted the land for mild dairy being shifted from city zone to rural zone on 20.09.2004 to the concerned persons @ Rs.
2500 per square mtr. in the village Ghoga which is adjacent to village Mubarakpur Dabas and the cost of the said land is Rs. 500 per square metre, therefore, it is not possible that there is so much difference in purchasing the land in the same area and location.

The MCD/DDA is earning uncountable profits by LAC no. 105/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ram Narain v. Union of India Page no. 7 of 15 incurring a little amount on the pretext of development, which is five times higher than the actual market price.

It is stated that the said land is adjacent to the developed industrial area of Bawana, developed by DSIDC having market value of the land between Rs. 4000 - Rs. 5000 per square metre, however, the land of the petitioner has been valued for Rs. 500 per square yards which is discriminatory in itself.
It is and infringement of right of property as laid down in Article 300, that no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.

8. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1/UOI and, it is, inter alia, submitted the present petition is not maintainable as the petitioner has failed to furnish any evidence in respect of the relief claimed in the present petition.

sentences.text: I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue wise findings and determination are as under: 
1.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to the enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount?
16. The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioners.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
17.

entities.text: State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To prove their case, the petitioners, through his counsel has adopted the evidence led in case Savitri Devi (supra).

During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned LAC no. 105/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ram Narain v. Union of India Page no. 12 of 15 case on 05.09.2023 and Ld.

entities.text: Ram Narain v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Counsel for the petitioners have argued that the petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioner in the aforementioned case.
18. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

19. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Mubarakpur Dabas and covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.

In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value as awarded in the case of Savitri Devi (supra) in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

20. In the case of Savitri Devi (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Mubarkpur Dabas acquired through Award No. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 as Rs. 19,45,800/
per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs. 3,75,800/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Savitri Devi (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Savitri Devi (supra).

This court adjudicate the market LAC no. 105/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ram Narain v. Union of India Page no. 13 of 15 value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.
21.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
No notice for taking the position has been LAC no. 105/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ram Narain v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 15 given to the petitioners, therefore, the petitioners have suffered loss on account of destruction of his crops.
It is the duty of the LAC to take into consideration every intrinsic Ram Narain (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 6 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180654263/
3 quality and intrinsic circumstances which tends to push the value either up or down.
(v) The learned LAC has not taken into account the market value which has been fixed by the Government and to be charged from the allottees of the residential plot/flats.
The market value was fixed by the Government at the time of notification under Section 4 of the Act without adjustment of amount towards the development charges, however, on the contrary, market value should have been assessed after taking into account the development charges.
The DDA has issued the guidelines/circulars showing the statement of market rates or charging unearned increase for the Colonies under the control of DDA year wise, however, the assessment of market value of the said land has been taken without consideration of the guidelines.
The DDA LAC no. 105/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ram Narain v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 15 and the said land has raised the rate of alternative plots from Rs. 750 per square yards to Rs. 4000 per square yards,
therefore, it is clear that the rates were increased by DDA and the said land has a very high potential value, which is evident from the said effect, that the price of the said land has increasing trend as regarding its market value and after afixation of the rate of agricultural land in Delhi, the prices of the said land has been increased by almost five times.
(vi) The learned LAC has also made grave error by not calling the petitioners for negotiation and the decision has been taken arbitrarily which is against the principles of natural justice.
Ld. LAC has assessed the fair market value of the said land by taking into consideration the prevailing market rates of the land at the time of notification U/s 4 of LA Act.
The possession of the land in question measuring 12 Bighas 04 Biswas as also detailed in the statement under Section 19 of LA Act only has been taken over by vide possession proceedings dated 04.04.2006 and the same has been handed over to DDA and DDA is therefore, a necessary party.
LAC no. 105/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ram Narain v. Union of India Page no. 10 of 15 11.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioners.
The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
17.

Whether the petitioner is entitled to the enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount?

opennyai_summary.decision:
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Savitri Devi (supra).
This court adjudicate the market LAC no. 105/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ram Narain v. Union of India Page no. 13 of 15 value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.
21.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
As per the reference petition forwarded by LAC, the possession of land bearing Khasra No. 14//9 (4-16), 12 (4-16), 19 (4-16), 29//4 (4-16), 6(4-12) and 7(4-16), has not been taken which has been admitted by the petitioner.
Therefore, petitioner is not entitled for enhancement of compensation qua this land.
23. In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs: (1) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.
(2)
Additional amount @ 12% ( in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).
(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
LAC no. 105/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ram Narain v. Union of India Page no. 14 of 15 24.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
